notes.meaning: Once the Sabbath day of rest ended at sundown, three faithful women bought spices to care for Jesus. They planned to anoint His body—rubbing it with fragrant oils—to honor Him and help cover the smell of decay. Their loving errand shows they cared deeply for Jesus, even though they did not yet realize He would rise from the dead.

The women started out at dawn and arrived at the burial cave just after sunrise on Sunday morning. This was the first day of the Jewish work week, and the third day since Jesus died on the cross. Their early trip showed their eager devotion to honor their Lord without delay.

As they walked along, the women wondered who would roll away the heavy stone blocking the tomb entrance. That stone was far too large for them to move on their own. They did not know guards had been placed there, but their concern shows they expected Jesus' body to still be inside.

When the women looked up, they saw that the massive stone had already been rolled aside. God sent an angel to move the barrier before they arrived. The stone was moved not to let Jesus out, but to let witnesses look inside and see what God had done.

Going inside the tomb, the women saw a young man sitting on the right side dressed in a long white robe. This was an angel appearing in bright, youthful form to show heavenly purity. Seeing a heavenly messenger startled the women and filled them with alarm.

The angel told them not to be afraid, recognizing that they were looking for Jesus the Nazarene who was crucified. He announced that Jesus was alive again and no longer in the tomb. He then pointed to the empty shelf so they could see the proof with their own eyes.

The angel told the women to take the news to the disciples, especially mentioning Peter. Naming Peter was an act of mercy to assure him of pardon after he had denied knowing Jesus. The Lord promised to meet them in Galilee, keeping the exact word He had given them earlier.

Overcome with shock and trembling, the women hurried away from the tomb. They were so shaken and bewildered that they did not stop to talk to anyone along the road. Their deep awe and fear temporarily kept them silent until they reached the disciples.

After Jesus rose early on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene. Jesus had previously freed her from the control of seven demons, showing the power of His grace to transform lives. He honored this devoted follower by making her the first witness of His resurrection.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars note that verses 9–20 are missing from the oldest Greek manuscripts and differ in style, suggesting this long ending was added by early Christians to summarize Jesus' appearances.

notes.meaning: Mary went straight to the disciples, who were crying and mourning over the death of their Master. They felt crushed and alone because they believed their Lord was gone forever. Mary brought the message of hope directly into their deep sorrow.

When the disciples heard that Jesus was alive and that Mary had seen Him, they refused to believe it. Their grief was so heavy that her words sounded impossible to them. Their stubborn doubt shows they were cautious people who did not easily invent or accept a resurrection story.

Later that day, Jesus appeared in a different manner to two followers walking out into the countryside. He joined them on the road, but they did not recognize Him at first. He walked beside them and explained the Scriptures before revealing who He was.

The two travelers rushed back to Jerusalem to tell the rest of the followers what had happened. Even after hearing their story, the others still did not believe them. It took overwhelming personal proof to overcome their doubts and fears.

Jesus then appeared to the eleven apostles while they were sharing a meal. He corrected them firmly for their lack of faith and stubborn hearts because they had ignored the witnesses who saw Him alive. His rebuke showed that refusing good evidence is not wisdom, but hardened unbelief.

Jesus commanded His followers to go throughout the entire world and preach the gospel—the good news of His salvation—to all people. His message was no longer confined to one nation, but was meant for every human being. This command gave the church its mission to reach every land.

Jesus taught that anyone who trusts in Him and is baptized will receive salvation—rescue from the guilt and penalty of sin. Baptism serves as the outward public mark of genuine inward faith. Those who refuse to believe will be condemned, because rejecting Christ leaves no other way to be forgiven.

differ.view: Lutherans teach that baptism is a "means of grace"—an actual way God gives the Holy Spirit and forgives sins. Even so, they note that the end of Mark 16:16 blames only unbelief for condemnation, so lacking water does not by itself keep someone out of heaven if they have true faith in Christ.

This evangelical Bible ministry explains that Mark 16:16 describes what normally happens to believers who are baptized, but it does not make baptism a requirement for heaven. Because the text never says that an unbaptized person is condemned, only personal trust in Jesus decides whether someone is saved.

notes.meaning: Jesus promised that miraculous signs would accompany believers to confirm the truth of the gospel. In His name they would drive out evil spirits and speak in new languages they had never studied. These powers helped launch the early church and showed that God was at work.

differ.view: These miracles were most likely given for a time, to support the gospel while it was new, and believers today should not expect them.

notes.meaning: Jesus promised protection from deadly snakes and poisons, and said believers would place hands on sick people to heal them. This was not an excuse to take foolish risks, but a pledge of God's protection during danger while serving Him. The early apostles experienced these very miracles as they spread the message.

differ.view: These miracles were most likely given for a time, to support the gospel while it was new, and believers today should not expect them.

notes.meaning: After the Lord Jesus finished speaking to His followers, He was taken up into heaven. He sat down at the right hand of God, which is the position of highest honor, rest, and rule. Having finished His earthly suffering, He took His place to govern all things in glory.

The disciples went everywhere preaching the good news just as Jesus told them to do. The Lord worked alongside them from heaven, confirming their message with powerful signs. Their obedience planted the Christian church across the ancient world.
